props.covers: The 20 grid is geometry quantization: every number a gesture writes to board geometry lands on a multiple of 20, while spacing is chosen from content and repeated peer geometry rather than from a grid-derived target.

text.insert: Object geometry uses the agent's 20 grid as a snap unit. It does not prescribe a gap, corridor width, or pitch: choose those for the content and flow, then express the resulting rectangles on-grid.

tells the agent to work in grid units and to match peers exactly: match_size copies a peer's dimensions, and every other coordinate comes from exact digest geometry. The gesture tools run every geometry-bearing value through

before it is lowered onto a document patch, and they snap rather than refuse: an off-grid value is corrected to the nearest multiple and the result reports the geometry that landed, so a correction is something the agent reads back rather than something it is told about. Not every number is a world distance — an endpoint fraction and a label's position along a routed path stay off the grid — and
enumerates which fields quantize and which are exempt. R1 is that quantization and nothing more: it decides where a number lands, never how much air the layout gets.
Operational check: a geometry patch supplies the complete finite
rectangle. Operation results and looks report the post-snap geometry in their digest rows, which is the value to read when matching peers.
